title: Why Ancient Yews Keep Growing
titleZh: 古老的紫杉为何生生不息
paras: In an old burial ground, a hollow yew can appear less like a living organism than a monument. Visitors may feel [[nostalgia|nostalgia]] for ceremonies once held beneath its branches, yet its survival requires no supernatural explanation. Although a village legend might credit a [[prophet|prophet]], believed to convey divine messages, the tree's persistence depends on its unusual capacity for renewal.

As the central wood decays, living tissue beneath the bark can continue transporting water and sugars. Branches touching damp soil may produce roots, while [[slender|slender]] shoots develop into substantial new stems. Calling such a tree a single individual therefore needs [[elaboration|elaboration]]: its original trunk may be disappearing even as connected younger structures extend its life.

This process complicates human attempts to manage ancient trees. A gardener wishing to [[cultivate|cultivate]] flowers nearby may damage shallow roots through digging, while removing apparently untidy branches can interrupt natural regeneration. A conservationist may consequently become the gardener's [[antagonist|antagonist]], opposing improvements intended to honour the site. Where protective rules apply, even well-meant pruning may [[violate|violate]] them; a prominent [[placard|placard]] can explain why deliberate neglect is sometimes careful management.

The yew's chemistry offers another reason for respect, though not for casual experimentation. Its poisonous tissues contain compounds from which medicines have been developed to inhibit the growth of a [[tumour|tumour]]. Eating any part is no substitute for medical treatment. It is therefore [[fitting|fitting]] that a tree associated with remembrance should also illuminate biological survival: what looks exhausted from outside may retain remarkable resources for continued life.
zh: 在一处古老的墓地里，一棵中空的紫杉看上去可能更像一座纪念碑，而不是活着的生命。游客或许会因昔日在树荫下举行的仪式而生出怀旧之情，但它的存续并不需要超自然的解释。即使村中的传说可能将其归功于一位被认为能传达神谕的先知，这棵树的长久生命仍取决于它非同寻常的自我更新能力。
当树干中心的木质部分腐朽时，树皮下的活组织仍能继续输送水分和糖分。接触潮湿土壤的枝条可能生根，细长的新梢则会长成粗壮的新树干。因此，将这样的树称为单一的个体，需要进一步说明：原来的树干可能正在消失，而与之相连的年轻结构却在延续它的生命。
这一过程使人们管理古树的工作变得复杂。想在附近栽种花卉的园丁可能在挖土时损伤浅层树根，而剪去看似杂乱的枝条则可能阻断自然更新。因此，自然保护者可能成为园丁的反对者，抵制那些本意是向这片场所致敬的改造。在适用保护规定的地方，即使出于善意的修剪也可能违规；一块醒目的告示牌可以解释，为何有意不加干预有时反而是一种细致的管理。
紫杉的化学特性提供了另一个值得敬重它的理由，却绝不是让人随意尝试的理由。它有毒的组织中含有某些化合物，人们以此为基础开发出了抑制肿瘤生长的药物。食用紫杉的任何部分都不能代替医疗。因此，一种与追思相联系的树也能帮助我们理解生命的延续，实在恰如其分：外表看似衰竭的生命，内部或许仍保有令人惊叹的生存资源。

q.s: Decay in the centre of a yew's trunk necessarily stops water transport beneath its bark.
q.why: 中心腐朽时，树皮下的活组织仍可输送水分。

q.s: Removing apparently untidy branches can disrupt an ancient yew's natural regeneration.
q.why: 第三段明确指出剪去这些枝条可能阻断更新。

q.s: Medicines derived from yew compounds are less expensive than other cancer treatments.
q.why: 末段介绍药用价值，未比较治疗费用。
